newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian rebels seeking young girls kill families.
newsitem.headline: Algerian rebels seeking young girls kill families.

text.p: Suspected Moslem fundamentalists killed between nine and 12 members of two families -- including four children -- in an attack aimed at kidnapping young girls, two Algerian newspapers said on Saturday.
El Watan said nine people died in Cheraifia, Boufarik region, Blida province, in a night-time raid by two groups each made up of about a dozen "terrorists".
Al Khabar, the main Arabic language newspaper, said 12 people were killed,
El Watan said the rebels moved into Cheraifia, some 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, at about 1 a.m. (midnight GMT) on Thursday and used knives to kill four children, three women and two men.
Eyewitnesses told the newspaper that the members of the Arrar and Djilali families were killed after the attackers broke down the doors of their homes in an attempt to kidnap teenage girls.
The youngest was 14 and the oldest 18, the newspaper said, adding that the attackers killed the family members when they tried to prevent the girls being dragged off.
El Watan said the arrival of local militia prevented the kidnap. Al Khabar said the attackers had succeeded in taking the five girls with them.
Moslem fundamentalists fighting to topple the authorities have previously kidnapped young women and forced them to go through a form of what they call "temporary marriage".
El Watan also said that four gunmen on Thursday shot dead a 23-year-old university student in the Algiers suburb of Beausejour.
She was shot twice in the face and twice in the stomach as she was leaving her home. The gunmen fled with her student bag.
About 60,000 people have been killed in more than five years of violence which erupted when the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election dominated by Islamic fundamentalists.
Algeria held new multi-party general elections earlier this month and the new parliament is due to hold its first session on Sunday.
